metadata.caption: Flow Chart of Proofs

nodes.name: Lemma D.21: $M()$ samples correctly from joint dist
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a sampling network for random variables $\{V_1, V_2,\hdots V_n\}$ formed by a collection of conditional generative models $M_{V_i}$ relative to $P(\mathbf{v})$ for all $V_i$. Then the tuple $(V_1, V_2\hdots V_n)$ obtained by sequentially evaluating each conditional generative model relative to the topological order of the sampling graph is a sample from the joint distribution $\Pi_i P_i(v_i|pa_i)$.

nodes.name: Lemma D.15: data sampled from same distribution as ID
nodes.statement:
Consider recursive calls  $ID(\mathbf{Y}, \mathbf{X}, G, P_{ID}(\mathbf{v}))$ and  \text{ID-GEN}\xspace$(\mathbf{Y}, \mathbf{X}, G, \mathcal{D}, {{\hat{\mathbf{X}}}}, {\hat{{G}}})$\xspace at any recursion level $R$. 
		If $\mathcal{D}[{\hat{\mathbf{X}}}, V] \sim P_{\text{ID-GEN}\xspace}({\hat{\mathbf{x}}}, \mathbf{v})$, then$P_{ID}(\mathbf{v}) = P_{\text{ID-GEN}\xspace}(\mathbf{v}|{\hat{\mathbf{x}}})$
		for fixed values of ${\hat{\mathbf{X}}}={\hat{\mathbf{x}}}$.

nodes.name: Lemma D.13: Same graph $G$ as ID
nodes.statement:
Consider the recursive calls  $ID(*, G_{ID})$ and  $\text{ID-GEN}\xspace(*,  G_{\text{ID-GEN}\xspace}, {\hat{\mathbf{X}}}, {\hat{{G}}} )$ at any level of the recursion.
		Then $G_{ID} = G_{\text{ID-GEN}\xspace}$ and $G_{ID}= {\hat{{G}}} \setminus {\hat{\mathbf{X}}}$.

nodes.name: Lemma D.14: ID 's relation with input $P(V)$
nodes.statement:
Let $P(.)$ be the input observational distribution to the ID algorithm and $\mathcal{D} \sim P(.)$ be the input observational dataset to the \text{ID-GEN}\xspace algorithm. 
		Suppose, ${\hat{\mathbf{X}}}$ is the set of variables that are intervened at step 7 of both the ID and \text{ID-GEN}\xspace algorithm from recursion level $R=0$ to $R=r$.
		Consider recursive calls  $ID(*, P_{ID}(\mathbf{v}))$ and  $\text{ID-GEN}\xspace(*, \mathcal{D}, *,  {\hat{\mathbf{X}}}, {\hat{{G}}} )$ at recursion level $R=r$.
		Then $P_{ID} = P_{{\hat{\mathbf{x}}}}(\mathbf{v})$ and $\mathcal{D}[{\hat{\mathbf{X}}}, \mathbf{V}] \sim P_{{\hat{\mathbf{x}}}}({\hat{\mathbf{x}}}, \mathbf{v})$.

nodes.name: Lemma D.11: Same recursive trace as ID
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Recursive trace)}
	
	
	
		
		
		At any recursion level $R$,
		recursive call
		\text{ID-GEN}\xspace$(\mathbf{Y}, \mathbf{X},  \mathcal{D}, G, {{\hat{\mathbf{X}}}}, {\hat{{G}}} )$ enters Step $i$ if and only if 
		recursive call ID$(\mathbf{Y},\mathbf{X}, P, G)$ enters Step $i$, for any $i\in [7]$

nodes.name: Lemma D.17: Correctness of Step 1 Base
Lemma D.18: Correctness of Step 6 Base
nodes.statement:
\textbf{\text{ID-GEN}\xspace Base case (step 6):} 
  Let, at any recursion level of \text{ID-GEN}\xspace, the input dataset $\mathcal{D}[{\hat{\mathbf{X}}}, \mathbf{V}]$ is sampled from a specific joint distribution $P({\hat{\mathbf{X}}},\mathbf{V})$, i.e., 
  $\mathcal{D}[{\hat{\mathbf{X}}}, \mathbf{V}] \sim P({\hat{\mathbf{X}}},\mathbf{V})$ where ${\hat{\mathbf{X}}}$ is the set of intervened variables at step 7s.
  Given an identifiable interventional query $P_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{y})$ over a causal graph $G=(V, E)$,  suppose \text{ID-GEN}\xspace$(\mathbf{Y}, \mathbf{X}, G, \mathcal{D}, {{\hat{\mathbf{X}}}}, {\hat{{G}}})$\xspace immediately enters step 6 and returns $\mathcal{H}$. Then $\mathcal{H}$ is a valid sampling network for $P_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{y})$ with fixed consistent ${\hat{\mathbf{X}}}= {\hat{\mathbf{x}}}$.

nodes.name: Lemma D.20: Sampling net follows $G_{\pi}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a sampling network produced by \text{ID-GEN}\xspace from an identifiable query $P_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{y})$ over a graph $G$. If $G$ has the topological ordering $\pi$, then every edge in the sampling graph of $\mathcal{H}$ adheres to the ordering $\pi$.

nodes.name: Theorem D.22: soundness
nodes.statement:
\textbf{\text{ID-GEN}\xspace Soundness:} Let $P_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{y})$ be an identifiable query given the causal graph $G=(V, E)$ and that we have access to joint samples $\mathcal{D}\sim P(\mathbf{v})$. Then the sampling network returned by \text{ID-GEN}\xspace$(\mathbf{Y}, \mathbf{X}, G, \mathcal{D}, {{\hat{\mathbf{X}}}}, {\hat{{G}}})$\xspace
		correctly samples from $P_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{y})$ under Assumption D.5.

nodes.name: Lemma D.16: Correctness of Fail Case
nodes.statement: If a non-identifiable query is passed to it, \text{ID-GEN}\xspace will return \texttt{FAIL}.

nodes.name: Theorem D.23: completeness
nodes.statement: \text{ID-GEN}\xspace is complete.

nodes.name: Lemma D.12: Termination
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Termination:} Let $P_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{Y})$ be a query for causal graph $G=(\mathbf{V}, E)$ and 
$\mathcal{D}\sim P(\mathbf{V})$. Then the recursions induced by \text{ID-GEN}\xspace$(\mathbf{Y}, \mathbf{X}, G, \mathcal{D}, {{\hat{\mathbf{X}}}}, {\hat{{G}}})$\xspace terminate in either step 1, 5, or 6.
